laws.label: A part cannot appear before its precursor
laws.statement: Every develops_from edge goes strictly later in stage, and the relation is acyclic.
sources: genotype/fin-subtree.json, certified in lean/Delphi/Certificates/FinDevelopment.lean
genotype/fin-subtree.json, certified in lean/Delphi/Certificates/FinDevelopment.lean

laws.label: Sustained mechanical power is bounded by oxygen delivery (Fick) times efficiency
laws.statement: With cardiac output Q, arterial and venous O2 contents Ca ≥ Cv ≥ 0, oxycaloric equivalent E and muscular efficiency 0 ≤ η ≤ 1, aerobic mechanical power is η E Q (Ca − Cv) ≤ η E Q Ca ≤ E Q Ca. A sustained power supplied aerobically is at most η E Q Ca; sustained flight needing P_req = W v/(L/D) requires η E Q Ca ≥ P_req; climb under an aerobic supply is at most (η E Q Ca − P_req)/W. If demand and supply are power laws in size with the supply exponent below the demand exponent there is a size above which supply falls short (crossover), so Thompson's size limit holds for any supply exponent below 7/2 without the muscle premise.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
laws.statement: In an atmosphere where air density and oxygen partial pressure both fall with height, the minimum speed of lift-supported flight and the power to fly at it are nondecreasing in height, while the aerobic supply (with arterial content nondecreasing in partial pressure, as a Hill curve gives) is nonincreasing. Hence sustained flight possible at a height is possible at every lower height; above an infeasible height every height is infeasible, so the flyable set is an interval from the ground up to a ceiling; and a design that cannot fly at the ground cannot fly at any height. A larger lifting area lowers the power required at a fixed height.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.statement: Induced drag falls with aspect ratio; L/D depends on fin shape.

laws.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
laws.statement: For a finite graph of ontology terms with a body root, a level per node and part_of edges (part, whole): if every edge goes strictly down in level, every edge joins two nodes, and every non-root node has a whole, then part_of is acyclic (its transitive closure is transitive and strictly decreases the level, so nothing is part of itself) and every node reaches the root. With pinned taxon statements: no never_in_taxon on a kept term, a superclass or a whole names a taxon containing the blueprint taxon, and every in_taxon or stated_in_taxon names a containing taxon. A Boolean checker decides all of this, and its truth implies the well-formedness (wellFormed_of_check); each emitted blueprint gets a certificate the kernel evaluates by decide.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.statement: Bones thicken with size (d ∝ ℓ^(3/2)) rather than isometrically.

laws.label: Fixation is at least i/M when selection does not oppose the mutant
laws.statement: In an absorbing chain on 0..M gene copies whose expected copy number never decreases (neutral, or selection for the mutant), a lineage present in i copies is eventually fixed with probability at least i/M. Wright-Fisher sampling with mutant relative fitness 1+s, s >= 0, is such a chain. Hence the expected number of substitutions over T generations is at least mu T (and at most M mu T), whatever M.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.statement: O2 delivered to tissue = cardiac output × (arterial − venous O2 content).
What sets pectoral fin length relative to body length (0.687 measured, Daane 2021).

laws.label: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)
laws.statement: The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.
sources: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)

laws.label: General allometry: measured exponents compose (W = a L^b)
laws.statement: For power laws f L = a L^b with real exponents: the ratio between two sizes is (L2/L1)^b, the log-log exponent is b, a quotient of power laws is a power law with exponent b1 − b2 (so wing loading W/S has exponent bW − bS), the cube law is the case b = 3, and under power laws for weight and lifting area with constant ρ and C_L,max the minimum-speed exponent is (bW − bS)/2.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: Climb from excess power and the range of a steady glide
laws.statement: If available mechanical power is spent on level flight, on raising the weight at vertical speed c, and on non-negative losses, then c ≤ (P_avail − P_req)/W. A steady glide with no thrust, lift equal to weight and L/D ≤ (L/D)max from height h covers at most h (L/D)max horizontally; with drag reduced by a fraction δ near the surface and lift unaffected, at most h (L/D)max/(1 − δ).
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.statement: How a gene edit changes a structure quantitatively (bioelectric kcnk5b, slc43a2a transport).

laws.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
laws.statement: Taking the developmental stage as the level of a blueprint graph whose edges are develops_from, the Boolean check devOrderedB is true exactly when every edge goes strictly down in stage; its truth implies that every derivative is staged strictly after its precursor and that develops_from is acyclic. The fin subtree's own edges are certified by a kernel evaluation of the checker on the recorded stages (lean/Delphi/Certificates/FinDevelopment.lean).
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
laws.statement: With the standard genetic code as a 64-codon table and minSubst a b the least number of positions in which a codon for a and a codon for b differ, no codon pair turns a into b in fewer than minSubst a b nucleotide substitutions. A claim of n substitutions with n < minSubst a b is therefore impossible. minSubst is computed over the table, so the kernel evaluates each instance: Phe to Leu takes 1, Trp to Stop 1, Met to Trp 2.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
laws.statement: The Boolean check closureB mapped changed is true exactly when every node in the mapped list occurs in the changed list; its truth implies the inclusion (closure_of_check), and a single mapped node absent from the changed list makes it false (closure_violated). Applied to the genotype map: a view that shows an edit to a gene changing fewer nodes than the map links to that gene is ruled out.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: The time N independent substitutions need lies between N/(M mu) and N/mu
laws.statement: With M gene copies, mutation rate mu per copy per generation and fixation probability u, the expected time for N substitutions arriving at Kimura's rate M mu u is N/(M mu u); for 1/M <= u <= 1 it lies between N/(M mu) and N/mu, and equals N/mu in the neutral case u = 1/M. An available time below N/(M mu), the fastest the model allows because it assumes every single mutant fixes, is ruled out.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.statement: Arterial O2 content as a function of water O2, gill area and ventilation (the first link of the simulator chain).

laws.label: From Haldane's cost accounting (a hypothesis, not proved here): N substitutions need at least c N / e generations
laws.statement: HaldaneCost N T e c is the NAMED HYPOTHESIS that N substitutions by selection in T generations cost at most e T / c, with reproductive excess e > 0 and cost per substitution c > 0. From it, T is at least c N / e, and a stated time below c N / e contradicts the hypothesis. The hypothesis itself is never proved.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele
laws.statement: The probability that a mutant allele eventually fixes in a finite population depends on its initial frequency, its selective advantage and the effective population size, and equals its initial frequency when it is neutral.
sources: On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population (1962)

laws.label: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate
laws.statement: For neutral mutations the long-run rate of molecular substitution equals the mutation rate per generation, independent of population size, which yields a molecular clock.
sources: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level (1968)

laws.label: Twofold cost of sex
laws.statement: An asexual mutant female in a sexual population with equal sex ratio produces twice as many grandchildren as a sexual female, so sex needs a compensating advantage of up to twofold to persist.
sources: The Evolution of Sex (1978)

laws.statement: Power available = f p M with muscle fraction f and mass-specific power p constant (Thompson 1917, ch. II).

laws.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
laws.statement: For a thin-walled sphere the wall stress is P r / (2 t) and for a cylinder P r / t; at fixed pressure and thickness the stress grows with radius, and a wall that holds at most sigma_max limits the pressure to 2 sigma_max t / r (sphere) or sigma_max t / r (cylinder).
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
laws.statement: For a rate X(T) = X0 Q10^((T - Tref)/10) with X0 nonzero and Q10 > 0, the ratio X(T2)/X(T1) is Q10^((T2 - T1)/10), and the log of that ratio is (T2 - T1)/10 times log Q10, so a Q10 fit is a straight line in log rate against temperature.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
laws.statement: In an isometric family an area scales as the square of the linear dimension, S(L2)/S(L1) = (L2/L1)^2, and with the cube law the weight per unit area (wing loading, or stress W/A) scales as L2/L1.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: Bending strength of an isometric member via the section modulus (R9)
laws.statement: For a slender linear-elastic beam the maximum bending stress is the moment over the section modulus, σ_b = F ℓ / Z. With similar sections (Z ∝ L^3) and a lever arm ∝ L: if the load scales as the body (F ∝ L^3, R9a) then σ_b scales as L, the bending safety factor σ_max/σ_b equals σ_max k_Z/(k_F k_ℓ L) and above L_max,b = σ_max k_Z/(k_F k_ℓ n) the member cannot carry n times its load; if the load scales as an area (a lamina of constant thickness, F ∝ L^2, R9b) then σ_b is independent of size and no size limit follows.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
laws.statement: A member of cross-section A made of material with breaking stress σ fails under axial load σ A. With isometric sections and the same material the breaking load scales as (L2/L1)^2, the static safety factor F_break/W equals σ k3/(k1 L) and falls as 1/L, stress W/A grows as L, and above L_max = σ k3/(k1 n) the member cannot carry n body weights.
sources: proved in this project; no paper states it in this form

laws.statement: Thrust from the caudal fin during taxiing, which the field glide distances require beyond one unpowered glide.

laws.label: Power needed for flight grows as length^3.5 while muscle power grows as length^3
laws.statement: A bird of fixed proportions must fly at a minimum speed proportional to the square root of its linear size, so the work needed for flight varies as the 3½ power of linear size while the work its muscles can supply varies only as the cube; flight thus becomes harder as birds get larger (about 1.4 times harder per doubling of length).
sources: On Growth and Form (1917)

laws.label: Ostrich and moa have passed the size at which muscular flight is possible
laws.statement: The ostrich probably, and the moa certainly, reached a size at which flight by muscular action with ordinary bird anatomy became physiologically impossible, and a bird as large as a man could not fly.
sources: On Growth and Form (1917)

laws.label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
laws.statement: Leaving aside differences in mechanical construction, swimming (Froude's law), flight (minimum stable speed) and walking (the leg swinging as a pendulum) all give the same result: an animal's velocity tends to vary as the square root of its linear dimensions.
sources: On Growth and Form (1917)

laws.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
laws.statement: Whatever the law of increase in a linear dimension, volume and therefore weight tend to vary as the cube of linear dimensions, which mainly (though not wholly) explains why the human weight curve differs in shape from the stature curve.
sources: On Growth and Form (1917)

laws.statement: Walking speed ∝ √L from the leg as a pendulum (Thompson ch. II, third route).

scope: Static mirror generated by dashboard/build-lean-api.mjs from lib/lean-source.mjs, the same loader the MCP tools (lean_laws_list, lean_law_get, lean_lawset_get) use. A law's status is a registry decision, not a truth value; "proved" means a Lean kernel proof about a model, never that the model describes an organism. Laws absent here are unchecked, not satisfied. Evaluation (lean_check) is not mirrored: the browser runs blueprint3d/browser-check.mjs locally via lean-client.js.
